data.title: Ethiopia vs Mozambique Prediction Tue 17 Nov: AI Panel Split
data.content:
This is the return leg of a back-to-back, played four days after Ethiopia's 1-0 win in Maputo. Kenean Markneh scored in the 87th minute after a goalless first half. The experts broadly agree on the facts. Mozambique had most of the ball and created the better chances, including the woodwork and saves. Ethiopia defended in a low block and won on a late transition. My web search added nothing newer about team news, so I have not assumed any new absences. ## What does the AI predict for Ethiopia vs Mozambique?

As of 16 November 2026, ScoreGPT's AI panel is split on Ethiopia vs Mozambique (AFCON Qualification): no single result leads among the 5 models, so there is no consensus call. Key factors: Ethiopia scored once in three qualifiers; Mozambique dominated but wasted chances. Every pick is graded publicly after full-time — for information and entertainment only. [...] Away-win camp (Grok, GPT): Mozambique's chance creation was better than the scoreline, and the Maputo finishing was an anomaly. They also have the higher attacking ceiling, with a 4-1 win over Sudan and a 1-1 draw with Senegal.
 Home-lean (DeepSeek): Bahir Dar's altitude and crowd, Ethiopia's acclimatised domestic squad, and a rattled Mozambique after the coach's press-conference exit. This leans on narrative more than hard evidence.

data.title: Federal Register :: Order Under Sections 362 and 365 of the Public Health Service Act Continuing the Suspension of the R
data.content:
Comment: One commenter recommended CDC also restrict travel to the United States from Somalia, Haiti, Kenya, and Ethiopia.

Response: CDC notes that there is currently no epidemiological evidence indicating that Somalia, Haiti, or Ethiopia should be included in this order. CDC continues to monitor the situation in Kenya and will impose restrictions if warranted by the epidemiological evidence. [...] Uganda completed the 42-day enhanced monitoring period—defined as twice the maximum incubation period for Ebola (21 days) per international guidance—on August 27, 2026.  Prior to August 27, 2026, Uganda reported 20 confirmed cases of Ebola disease and two confirmed deaths, as well as one probable case and one probable death. The last confirmed case of the outbreak was reported on June 21, 2026. Of the confirmed cases, 15 were imported cases and 5 were secondary cases linked to imported cases [...] September 11, 2026, and October 11, 2026, respectively. During the comment period for the October 11, 2026, Order, CDC received eight comments, which are addressed below. With this notice, CDC is announcing the issuance of an Order that continues the suspension of the right to introduce certain persons who have departed from, or were otherwise present within, specified countries during the last 21 days. This Order is effective for a period of 30 days.
